extracted.intended_audience: persons or organizations (including non-U.S. citizens) preparing and submitting citizen petitions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (petitioners, counsel, stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a citizen petition under 21 CFR 10.30 to request FDA administrative action (issue/amend/revoke regulations or orders, or take/refrain from other administrative action). Covers required format, submission methods, contents, procedural timelines, recordkeeping, and review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to any petition submitted by a person (including a person who is not a citizen of the United States) except to the extent that other sections of this chapter apply different requirements to a particular matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates who may use this provision and that other, topic-specific sections may impose different requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must comply with general rules (§10.20 and §10.31 where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition (including any attachments) must be submitted in accordance with §10.20 and, if applicable, §10.31. The certification requirement in this section does not apply to petitions subject to the certification requirement of §10.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check and follow §10.20 (general submission requirements) and §10.31 (verification/certification) when preparing a petition; determine whether §10.31's certification applies so as to avoid duplicate or conflicting certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions (including any attachments) may be electronically submitted in accordance with paragraph (b)(3) of this section and §10.20 through http://www.regulations.gov at Docket No. FDA 2013-S-0610. It is only necessary to submit one copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission through regulations.gov is permitted and only one copy is required when submitted electronically; follow the petition format specified in paragraph (b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail/delivery submission and copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition (including any attachments) that is not electronically submitted must be submitted in accordance with paragraph (b)(3) and §10.20 and delivered to Dockets Management Staff at the specified Rockville, MD address. Submit two copies (original and redacted version) for confidential petitions; otherwise only one copy is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-electronic petitions must follow the format and receipt address; if confidential, provide both original and a redacted public copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition format — overall
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition submitted under paragraphs (b)(1) or (b)(2) must be in accordance with §10.20 and in the following format: include 'Citizen Petition', Date, statement of statutory basis, and the requested action. The petition must follow the labeled sections A–E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed labeled structure (A. Action Requested; B. Statement of Grounds; C. Environmental Impact; D. Economic Impact; E. Certification) and include the statutory authority and precise requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Requested (Section A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, include the exact wording of the existing regulation (if any) and the proposed regulation or amendment requested. If requesting issuance/amendment/revocation of an order, provide exact wording of the citation to the existing order (if any) and the exact wording requested. If requesting other administrative action, specify the specific action or relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the requested action with exact, word-for-word proposed regulatory or order language (or precise description of other relief) to enable clear implementation if approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Grounds (Section B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full statement, in a well-organized format, of the factual and legal grounds on which the petitioner relies, including all relevant information and views on which the petitioner relies, as well as representative information known to the petitioner which is unfavorable to the petitioner's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete, well-organized factual and legal justification; include all supporting data and explicitly disclose material adverse or unfavorable information known to the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact (Section C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide either a claim for categorical exclusion under §§25.30–25.34 of this chapter or an environmental assessment under §25.40 of this chapter, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include environmental documentation consistent with the cited NEPA-related regulations when relevant; identify the specific categorical exclusion or attach an environmental assessment if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic impact (Section D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic impact information is to be submitted only when requested by the Commissioner following review of the petition: a statement of the effect of requested action on cost (and price) increases to industry, government, and consumers; productivity of wage earners, businesses, or government; competition; supplies of important materials, products, or services; employment; and energy supply or demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include economic impact analysis unless requested; if requested, address each listed economic factor comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification (Section E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The undersigned certifies that, to the best knowledge and belief of the undersigned, this petition includes all information and views on which the petition relies, and that it includes representative data and information known to the petitioner which are unfavorable to the petitioner's position. Signature, name, mailing address, and telephone number must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the required signed certification and contact information; be truthful and disclose unfavorable information as part of the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing, docketing, and unique docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition that appears to meet format and submission requirements will be filed by the Dockets Management Staff, stamped with the date of filing, and assigned a unique docket number which identifies the docket file for all submissions relating to the petition. Subsequent submissions must refer to that docket number. Related petitions may be filed together and given the same docket number. The Dockets Management Staff will promptly notify the petitioner of the filing and unique docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all further submissions reference the assigned docket number; related matters may be consolidated under one docket number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments on filed petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may submit comments to the Dockets Management Staff on a filed petition; comments become part of the docket file, must specify the docket number, and include verification under §10.31 if applicable. Comments may support or oppose the petition in whole or in part. A request for alternative or different administrative action must be submitted as a separate petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party commenters must use the docket number and, if required by §10.31, include the verification; do not use comments to request alternative actions — file a separate petition for that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in Commissioner's ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall rule on each filed petition taking into consideration: (i) available agency resources for the category of subject matter, (ii) the priority assigned to the petition considering both the category of subject matter involved and the overall work of the agency, and (iii) time requirements established by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be aware that resource constraints, agency priorities, and statutory deadlines influence timing and handling of petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and types of response to petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in specified exceptions, the Commissioner shall furnish a response within 180 days of receipt. The response will either: (i) approve the petition (and take implementing action), (ii) deny the petition, (iii) dismiss the petition if rendered moot, or (iv) provide a tentative response explaining inability to reach a decision and possibly indicating likely ultimate response and when a final response may be furnished. Special timing: responses within 90 days for petitions filed under section 505(j)(2)(C); the Commissioner intends to respond within 150 days for petitions subject to section 505(q). Agency action on petitions governed by §314.93 where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a standard 180-day timeframe unless petition falls under statutory provisions requiring different timelines; tentative responses are permitted to explain delays and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's authority regarding grant/denial/dismissal and public disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may grant or deny a petition in whole or in part, grant other relief or take other action as the petition warrants, and dismiss petitions rendered moot. The petitioner will be notified of the decision. The decision will be placed in the public docket file and may also be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions may be partial; expect public posting of the decision and possible Federal Register notice. Notification to petitioner is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedures when petition requests regulatory change
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, §10.40 or §10.50 also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory-change petitions trigger additional procedural requirements cited in §§10.40/10.50 — consult those sections when requesting regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing, amending, or withdrawing a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition without Agency approval and without prejudice to resubmission at any time until the Commissioner rules on the petition, unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12–15. After a ruling or referral, a petition may be supplemented, amended, or withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner. The Commissioner may approve withdrawal, with or without prejudice against resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before a ruling (and if not referred for hearing) petitioners may freely change or withdraw petitions; after referral or ruling, Commissioner approval is required and withdrawal may carry conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures the Commissioner may use in reviewing a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: In reviewing a petition the Commissioner may use: (1) conferences, meetings, discussions, and correspondence under §10.65; (2) a hearing under parts 12–16; (3) a Federal Register notice requesting information and views; (4) a proposal to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation in accordance with §10.40 or §12.20; and (5) any other specific public procedure established in this chapter and expressly applicable to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review may include informal meetings, formal hearings, public notice-and-comment, regulatory proposal procedures, or other specified public procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding consists of: (1) the petition, including all information on which it relies; (2) all comments received on the petition; (3) if the petition resulted in a proposal to issue/amend/revoke a regulation, all documents specified in §10.40(g); (4) the record consisting of transcripts, minutes, reports, Federal Register notices, and other documents from optional procedures, except transcripts of closed portions of a public advisory committee meeting; (5) the Commissioner's decision including all information identified or filed by the Commissioner with the Dockets Management Staff supporting the decision; (6) all documents filed under §10.65(h); and (7) if a petition for reconsideration or a stay is filed under paragraph (j), the administrative record specified in §10.33(k) or §10.35(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the administrative record aggregates filings, comments, procedural documents, and the Commissioner's decision and supporting materials; closed-session transcripts are excluded as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity of the administrative record and new information
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative record specified in paragraph (i) is the exclusive record for the Commissioner's decision. The record closes on the date of the Commissioner's decision unless some other date is specified. Thereafter any interested person may submit a petition for reconsideration under §10.33 or a petition for stay of action under §10.35. A person who wishes to rely upon information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the decision in accordance with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material not included in the administrative record cannot be used to challenge the decision; additional information must be submitted via a new petition (reconsideration or modification) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions — what this section does not cover (routine correspondence; referrals to U.S. attorneys)
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to the referral of a matter to a United States attorney for initiation of court enforcement action and related correspondence, or to requests, suggestions, and recommendations made informally in routine correspondence received by FDA. Routine correspondence does not constitute a petition within the meaning of this section unless it purports to meet the requirements of this section. Action on routine correspondence does not constitute final administrative action subject to judicial review under §10.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish formal petitions from informal or enforcement-referral correspondence; routine communications are not petitions unless they explicitly meet the petition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dockets Management Staff recordkeeping and public docket list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dockets Management Staff will maintain a chronological list of each petition filed under this section and §10.85 (but not petitions submitted elsewhere under §10.25(a)(1)), showing: (1) the docket number; (2) the date the petition was filed by the Dockets Management Staff; (3) the name of the petitioner; (4) the subject matter involved; and (5) the disposition of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition tracking information will be publicly maintained with specified fields; petitions filed under other provisions may not appear on this list.
